title: Rhombus-Shaped Absorbers for Parabolic Trough Solar Collectors: Concentration-Ratio Gains, Thermal–Hydraulic Trade-Offs, and Exergy Performance
content: Raising the concentration ratio (CR) of a parabolic trough collector (PTC) allows higher operating temperatures and smaller heat losses, but shrinking a circular absorber eventually lets reflected rays miss it. Secondary mirrors overcome this limit but shade the primary mirror. An alternative is to change the absorber shape. This paper analyzes the rhombus-shaped absorber, whose diagonals are sized to match the varying distance between the mirror and the focal line, and evaluates it against the conventional circular tube. Using the optical, thermal, and exergy results of a recent coupled ray-tracing and finite-volume study of a EuroTrough-type collector, the paper derives the geometric design relations, compares concentration, flux, temperature uniformity, pressure drop, and efficiency, and quantifies the net benefit after pumping power. For rim angles of 80° and 90°, the rhombus raises the CR by 16.1% and 31.5% without loss of optical efficiency and lowers the circumferential temperature difference from about 30 K to 20 K. It does so at the cost of a five- to elevenfold increase in pressure drop. At an inlet temperature of 650 K, thermal efficiency rises by up to 2.28%, exergy efficiency by up to 2.84%, and overall efficiency by up to 2.46%. The extra heat collected exceeds the electrical-equivalent pumping penalty by a wide margin. Manufacturing, thermal-stress, and field-validation needs are identified.
